title: M2 routing priorities
intro: The code review found three independent causes behind the Claude-heavy map: medium risk forces tier 1, Codex/Gemini quota evidence was stale, and the full-plan route map decides tasks independently. Please settle the policy before I draft the implementation plan. Recommendations are grounded in the current M1/M2 boundary and avoid live model calls.
coverage: 8/10 clear; routing priorities and quota refresh remain open

questions.text: Should `risk: medium` by itself keep raising every task to tier 1?

options.label: Yes; medium risk is a tier-1 floor
No; complexity and task kind set the base, with explicit high-risk/architecture/scope rules for uplift

questions.why: Six of seven REQ-017 tasks had medium risk, so this single rule raised five routine implementation tasks to Sonnet xhigh.

questions.text: When multiple routes meet the task floor, how should M2 rank providers and accounts?

options.label: Task fit and evidence first, then fresh per-account quota; include Gemini as a normal eligible builder, with measured latency as a ranking factor
Favor measured speed/quality; keep Gemini as audit/reserve and use quota mainly as a tie-break
Maximize quota headroom even when the route is slower or less proven

questions.why: This lets Codex and Gemini use real headroom without removing task floors or pretending the providers have equal speed/quality.

questions.text: Should the full DAG receive a joint account-aware recommendation instead of one independent decision per task?

options.label: Yes; allocate by task fit, fresh headroom, and known account capacity; no forced equal split; M1 revalidates before dispatch
Keep independent task recommendations, but show the selected profile/account
Spread tasks evenly across eligible accounts, even if headroom differs

questions.why: Each task already stores its profile/account, but independent recommendations can repeat the same account across the plan.

questions.text: Should the Scheduler request one bounded quota-only refresh before initial route planning and each READY batch?

options.label: Yes; refresh usage once per effective account outside M2 core; no model call; failed sources stay unavailable with a reason
No; use only the existing cache and exclude stale/unknown accounts
Keep refresh manual; require an operator preflight before every run

questions.why: M2 currently reads cached data, and the direct M1/M2 path bypasses the Antigravity refresh used by the legacy router; the Codex poll is currently failing.

q1.note: Inferred from the owner's instruction to use real complexity and multiple levels; medium risk alone should not promote every task.

q2.note: Owner explicitly wants quota and capable OpenAI/Codex and Gemini/Antigravity accounts considered; measured latency remains a ranking factor.

q3.note: Inferred from the earlier full-DAG request plus the current requirement to select a specific account per task.

q4.note: Implementation assumption for plan review, not a direct answer: refresh due quota once per effective account outside M2 core, with no model call.
